# 7470 - J-K flip-flop

Package DIP-14 · family 74 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/7470.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/7470.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 15 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![7470 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/7470.png) | ![7470 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/block-7470.png) | ![7470 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/block-7470.png) |

How to tell it on a drawing: Read the part type from the parts list and compare the pin numbers against this cut-out.

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | Q = state | Q is the stored bit (low while PR and CLR are both low). |
| 6 | /Q = NOT state | Q' is the inverse of the stored bit (low while PR and CLR are both low). |

## Stored state

Bits stored: 1

Changes on: rising edge of CK

- J = J1 AND J2 AND NOT J'; K = K1 AND K2 AND NOT K'
- PR low, CLR high, CK low: Q = 1, Q' = 0 at once
- PR high, CLR low, CK low: Q = 0, Q' = 1 at once
- PR low, CLR low (CK don't care): Q = 0 and Q' = 0 (table prints L* L*); not stable, does not persist when PR and CLR return high
- Preset or clear can occur only when CK is low
- PR high, CLR high, rising edge of CK: J=0 K=0 hold; J=1 K=0 Q=1; J=0 K=1 Q=0; J=1 K=1 toggle
- PR high, CLR high, CK low: hold

## Propagation delays

All measured at VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 15 pF, RL 400 ohm.

| From | To | Edge | Typ ns | Max ns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PR | Q | PLH |  | 50 |
| PR | /Q | PHL |  | 50 |
| CLR | /Q | PLH |  | 50 |
| CLR | Q | PHL |  | 50 |
| CK | Q | PLH | 27 | 50 |
| CK | Q | PHL | 18 | 50 |
| CK | /Q | PLH | 27 | 50 |
| CK | /Q | PHL | 18 | 50 |

| pulse width low | CLR |  | 25 |  |  |

## Not known

- Typical preset and clear propagation delays: the table gives the maximum (50 ns) only.

## Notes

The 7470 function table prints PR=L, CLR=L as Q = L, Q' = L (marked nonstable); the 7472/7474/7476 tables in the same book print H H for that case. The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delays; the path-delay function uses 0 ns for the minimum.
